tool.name: Text reformatting with awk over a collection
tool.description: one job for all elements, element identifier as a variable
tool.command: env -i \$(which awk) --sandbox -v FS=' ' -v OFS=' ' #for $i, $r in enumerate($variables, start=1) -v VAR$i='$r.value' #end for --re-interval -f '$awk_script' #if $lookup id='__lookup__' '$lookup' #end if #for $element in $input #set $identifier = str($element.element_identifier).replace("'", "") id='$identifier' '$element' #end for > '$outfile'

param.name: input
param.label: Collection to process
param.help: All elements are read by one awk process, in the order of the collection.

param.name: lookup
param.label: Lookup file read before the collection
param.help: Optional, for example a sample table to join with. While it is read, the variable id is __lookup__.

param.name: code
param.label: AWK program
param.help: The element identifier of the file being read is in the variable id. FS and OFS are TAB. BEGINFILE and ENDFILE run once per element.

param.name: value
param.label: Value
param.help: Available as VAR1, VAR2, ... in the program.

param.name: code
param.value: { n++ } ENDFILE { print id, n; n = 0 }

param.name: code
param.value: id == "__lookup__" { name[$1] = $2; next } FNR == 1 { print id, name[id], VAR1 }

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs one gawk program over every element of a list collection in a single job. While an element is read, its element identifier is in the variable ``id``, so per-sample results can carry the sample name without a separate "add input name as column" step and without concatenating the per-sample outputs afterwards.
This replaces chains such as *awk per element* followed by *add input name as column* and *concatenate*, which otherwise run as several jobs per element.
-----
**Program**
- ``FS`` and ``OFS`` are TAB. - ``id`` holds the element identifier of the file being read. - ``BEGINFILE`` and ``ENDFILE`` blocks run once per element; use them where a per-element program had an ``END`` block. - ``FNR`` counts lines within the element, ``NR`` over all elements. - An optional lookup file is read before the collection, with ``id`` set to ``__lookup__``. - Variables are available as ``VAR1``, ``VAR2``, ...
The program runs in gawk's sandbox mode: no ``system()``, no redirection, no reading of other files.
